chunk_text: KYC refresh failed because a beneficial-ownership event was not propagated from the client master into the periodic-review queue. The scheduler itself was healthy. Operations must repair event propagation, replay affected ownership events, and recalculate review due dates. The visible symptom was a missed refresh, but the control failure was the broken event-to-review linkage. The control owner must document the decision, preserve supporting evidence, and use the effective procedure version applicable to the event date. Similar records may appear in the same operational queue, so analysts should verify the precise trigger and scope before selecting a response. Exceptions must follow the approved escalation path and should not be inferred from shared terminology alone.
